_comment: Single source of truth for gray-area's local tool dependencies. Consumed by the shared toolchain probe, used by /prosthetic-conscience:doctor. Gray Area reads trajectories that the harness already writes, so it declares only what it must SHELL OUT to: git, and ripgrep for full-text search across those trajectories.

tools.name: ripgrep
tools.purpose: full-text search across every local trajectory. Measured on this repository's own corpus (282 MB, 385 transcripts): 33-54 ms for a whole-corpus search, against an estimated 1-2 GB for an FTS5 index that would also need invalidating on every append and rebuilding whenever the vendor deletes a session. The filesystem is already the index and cannot go stale, so gray-area shells out rather than building one. NOTE for anyone testing this by hand inside Claude Code: `rg` there is a shell FUNCTION the client injects (`exec -a rg $CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH`), not a binary — `bash -c 'command -v rg'` fails while an interactive `rg` appears to work, so a hand-run measurement can be taken through a path no Go program can use. toolchain.Probe uses exec.LookPath on the first token and so correctly refuses the function, which is why this entry is needed even on a box where `rg` seems present.
tools._tier_comment: REQUIRED AS OF THE `telepathy find` VERB. This entry was deliberately ahead of its consumer while the search verb was a draft plan: `required` returns BLOCKED, and blocking an install for a capability nothing used would have been a door where a nudge was wanted, so it sat at `recommended` (DEGRADED). The verb now ships, and from that moment ripgrep's absence stops being an inconvenience: `telepathy find` shells out to it, and a search that cannot run reports the same empty result as one that ran and matched nothing (facts-are-fields clause 3 — the miss must not fold into the honest zero). The binary refuses the search out loud rather than returning that zero, and this tier is what stops a consumer reaching that refusal at all.

install.linux: sudo apt-get install -y ripgrep (or the distro equivalent)

tools.name: git
tools.purpose: version control; inspections are declared against a tracked tree

_hook_binaries._comment: OUR compiled hooks, not external deps — one per directory under tools/cmd/. /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix fetches the CI-built release asset <name>_{goos}_{goarch}{exe} (SHA256-verified) into bin/, falling back to go build only as a dev convenience. hooks.json invokes ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/<name>.

binaries.name: gray-area-capture
binaries.purpose: two jobs on four events. SubagentStop and SessionStart write the MANIFEST — one row per seat naming that seat's own agent_transcript_path, an index and never a copy of conversation content. Stop and SessionEnd write NO manifest row at all: they exist for the CATALOGUE, reading the ending session's own transcript into the host-wide store telepathy queries, and SessionStart additionally closes out sessions that have stopped since and prunes past the retention window. A turn boundary is not a seat, which is why those two are explicit branches rather than additions to the seat-row path. Never blocks a session: every catalogue failure is reported on stderr and swallowed.

binaries.name: gray-area
binaries.purpose: the miner: lists tool invocations with provenance and resolves shell-aliased calls; refuses to emit a row it cannot cite

binaries.name: telepathy
binaries.purpose: the switchboard: what every agent on this box did, said and thought, queryable by any other session. Gray Area is the plugin; telepathy is the act, which is why it is its own binary rather than more verbs on `gray-area` — that one adjudicates ONE trajectory against a document, this one reads across the host. Every absence it prints is worded, because no store, no rows, no sessions and no captured reasoning are four different facts
